title: Bioinformatics Specialist
details: Public Health Sciences Division · Matsen Lab
summary: Conceptualized and implemented transformer-based deep amino acid selection models (DASM) of viral protein evolution in PyTorch. Designed and built multidms, a JAX model that jointly fits multiple deep mutational scanning datasets, now used in primary analysis pipelines across multiple labs. Built a Nextflow pipeline that ran 50K+ HPC jobs to produce the primary data for a study published in *Cell*.

highlights.title: Deep selection models for viral protein evolution
highlights.text: Conceptualized and implemented a Deep Amino acid Selection Model (DASM) for viral protein evolution. It adapts the lab's transformer framework for separating natural selection from mutation, originally built for B-cell lineages, to viral phylogenies. Built the codon-level training objective and the parent-child data pipeline in PyTorch within the open-source [netam](https://github.com/matsengrp/netam) package. This work is not yet published.

highlights.title: Jointly modeling deep mutational scanning (DMS) datasets
highlights.text: Developed a new approach for jointly modeling multiple DMS datasets, validated both *in silico* on simulated data and *in vitro* by testing mutations in the lab. Implemented it as a functional API in [multidms](https://matsengrp.github.io/multidms/), a JAX-based Python package [@Haddox_2023] now used in primary analysis pipelines across multiple labs.

highlights.title: Bioinformatics for studying affinity maturation in germinal centers
highlights.text: Worked with wet-lab researchers to build an efficient Nextflow pipeline that used high-performance computing clusters and software containers to run more than 50K independent data-processing steps and produce 140+ feature-rich phylogenetic trees. The pipeline produced the primary data and analysis for a large study spanning multiple groups, since published in *Cell* [@DeWitt_2025].

highlights.title: Administrative data management
highlights.text: Managed and stored sensitive data according to best practices across computational environments, including HPC file systems and AWS S3 buckets. Scrubbed sensitive data from repository histories before publication.

highlights.title: Visualizing and communicating results
highlights.text: Visualized data for researchers and produced publication figures that communicate patterns clearly. Regularly presented the background and results of my research at lab, collaborator, and team meetings.

title: Bioinformatics Analyst II
details: Public Health Sciences Division · Matsen Lab
summary: Designed an algorithm that estimates fitness over time for every codon mutation across a phylogeny of 13M+ viral genomes. Built and deployed public Nextstrain views of antibody escape for SARS-CoV-2, influenza, and Lassa virus. Mentored interns, students, and postdocs in ML and computational methods.

highlights.title: Algorithmic design for mutational fitness estimation
highlights.text: Designed and implemented an algorithm, packaged as a Snakemake pipeline, that estimates fitness trajectories over time for every possible codon mutation across a phylogeny (evolutionary history) of more than 13 million viral genomes.

highlights.title: Genomic surveillance of viral escape
highlights.text: Built and deployed custom public Nextstrain pages for viruses including [SARS-CoV-2](https://nextstrain.org/groups/dms-phenotype/ncov/Dadonaite-2023-Cell), influenza, and Lassa, each estimating viral escape from antibodies of interest. These pages have supplied analysis tools for several studies and helped assess the antibodies' potential as therapeutics.

highlights.title: Mentoring
highlights.text: Mentored undergraduate interns, graduate students, and postdocs, and onboarded new staff in machine learning, algorithm implementation, HPC clusters, workflow management, version control, compute environments, and build systems.

title: Research Associate
details: Paid Internship · Computational Biology · Matsen Lab
summary: Built phippery, a PhIP-Seq analysis suite (Nextflow pipeline, Python API for normalization and enrichment statistics, Streamlit app) used in six collaborative publications. Co-developed torchdms, a PyTorch package for neural-network global epistasis models. Led cross-lab team meetings.

highlights.title: PhIP-Seq software and analysis
highlights.text: Developed [phippery](https://matsengrp.github.io/phippery/introduction.html), a software suite for analyzing raw Phage ImmunoPrecipitation Sequencing (PhIP-Seq) data. It comprises a Python package for modeling and computing enrichment statistics, an interactive app for visualizing processed data, and an end-to-end (raw data → results) Nextflow pipeline that makes the standard analysis workflow portable and reproducible. Six collaborative publications have used it to process data and produce results [@Garrett_2022, @Stoddard_2021, @Garrett_2021, @Stoddard_2023, @Willcox_2022, @Itell_2021].

highlights.title: Neural networks for global epistasis modeling
highlights.text: Co-developed [torchdms](https://github.com/matsengrp/torchdms) with a graduate student: a PyTorch package that fits neural-network global epistasis models to deep mutational scanning data.

highlights.title: Team organization
highlights.text: Organized and led team meetings across multiple labs and studies to brainstorm, set short-term goals, and present results.

title: Graduate Teaching Fellow
details: BIO 410/510 · Biology Department · UO Graduate School
summary: Taught graduate-level Python/Bash scripting and algorithmic thinking. Built Docker containers and a Jupyter Notebook auto-grading pipeline. Led discussions and graded about 100 assignments per week.

highlights.title: Teaching
highlights.text: Led discussions, taught lessons, and proctored exams for four classroom hours each week in a graduate-level course on Python/Bash scripting, Unix file formats and parsing, and algorithmic thinking.

highlights.title: Assignment design
highlights.text: Built Docker containers and a Jupyter Notebook auto-grading pipeline that gave students a unified Python programming environment. Held office hours and graded about 100 assignments and exams per week, with feedback.

title: Scientific Programmer
details: Institute of Ecology and Evolution · Ralph & Kern Co-Lab
summary: Trained and evaluated recurrent neural networks on simulated genomes to estimate recombination rates (ReLERNN). Brought software engineering practice (architecture, version control, CI) to open-source tools including tskit and stdpopsim, and built Snakemake pipelines for published analyses.

highlights.title: Software engineering
highlights.text: Applied software engineering best practices, such as architecture design, version control, and continuous integration, to open-source projects including [tskit](https://tskit.dev/), [stdpopsim](https://popsim-consortium.github.io/stdpopsim-docs/stable/index.html), and [ReLERNN](https://github.com/kr-colab/ReLERNN).

highlights.title: Experimentation and model development
highlights.text: Trained recurrent neural networks (RNNs) on simulated data to predict recombination rates across the genomes of real populations, and evaluated how well they transfer from simulation to real data. This work provided the analysis pipeline for the resulting publication [@Adrion_2020_relernn].

highlights.title: Analysis of population demography inference tools
highlights.text: Built a Snakemake pipeline for a published comparison of population demography inference tools [@Adrion_2020_stdpopsim].

title: Undergraduate Research Assistant
details: Institute of Ecology and Evolution · Ralph & Kern Co-Lab
summary: Implemented tree-sequence recording in the SLiM population genetics simulator and benchmarked its speed and memory use for an honors thesis. Led a published simulation study of rapid evolution in stickleback fish.

highlights.title: Algorithmic implementation of tree-sequence recording
highlights.text: Implemented the tree-sequence recording algorithm in [SLiM](https://messerlab.org/slim/), a widely used population genetics simulator, and helped write the resulting publication [@Haller_2019].

highlights.title: Algorithmic benchmarking
highlights.text: Used cluster resources and visualization tools to compare large-scale simulations and benchmark performance on metrics including memory allocation and user runtime. Presented this work in my [undergraduate honors thesis](https://www.cs.uoregon.edu/Reports/UG-201806-Galloway.pdf); it also informed ongoing studies.

highlights.title: Simulation studies of rapid evolution
highlights.text: Developed and analyzed large-scale, realistic evolutionary simulation models to study migration patterns involved in the rapid evolution of stickleback fish on the Alaskan coast, and led the resulting publication [@Galloway_2020].

title: Discrete Math Course Grader
summary: Graded weekly discrete math assignments focused on proofs, set theory, and combinatorics.

highlights.title: Grading
highlights.text: Graded and wrote feedback on about 100 assignments each week, covering proofs, set theory, and combinatorics.
